title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloy composed of Mn, Ni, Si, Fe, Co, and Ge
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of Co for Fe in the (MnNi)Si(FeCo)Ge alloy system
recollection.structure: Likely a single-phase solid solution or multiphase structure typical of high-entropy alloys, possibly with a B2 or related structure
recollection.mechanism: Co substitution modifies the electronic and magnetic interactions, tuning the magnetocaloric effect by altering the magnetic transition temperature and entropy change
recollection.results: Enhanced magnetocaloric properties, such as increased magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) and/or improved refrigerant capacity, compared to the parent alloy without Co substitution; quantitative values would likely be in the range of several J/kg·K under a 2–5 T field change, but exact numbers are not recalled.

score.note: The recollection incorrectly states that Co substitutes for Fe; the study systematically substitutes Co for Ni. The proposed B2/single-phase structure is speculative and misses the Ni2In-type to TiNiSi-type transformation. The mechanism is only generic, omitting phase stabilization, Mn–Mn covalent bonding, and magnetostructural coupling. No actual numerical results are recalled, and the suggested entropy-change range substantially understates the peak value of 48.5 J kg−1 K−1 at 5 T.
